items.title: Philippines' Muslim self-ruled region facing hung parliament
items.summary: COTABATO: The Philippines' autonomous Muslim south appeared headed for a hung parliament on Tuesday, unofficial results showed, a day after landmark elections held amid scattered violence. About 83 per cent of eligible voters turned out for Monday's election, which the country's elections chief hailed as a success, calling residents of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, or BARMM, "fearless." The two top vote-getters – the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) and the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) – had earned about 35.2 and 32.4 per cent of the vote as of Tuesday evening.

items.title: Court orders family bungalow sold after 15-year sibling dispute
items.summary: Judge Arziah Mohamed Apandi said allowing the current arrangement to continue would leave one of the siblings unable to realise his share of the property, resulting in a "continuing injustice". The court ordered the bungalow, which is held for the equal benefit of Abdul Aziz Al-Akbar Mohamed Noor, 70, and his sisters, Jelinar Mohamed Noor, 65, and Shamsinar Mohamed Noor, 59, to be sold, with the net proceeds divided equally among them. In her written grounds dated Aug 13, Arziah said the evidence showed that the relationship between Abdul Aziz and Jelinar had broken down irretrievably.

items.title: DBKL steps up checks on outdoor dining
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will step up checks on walkways used for outdoor dining to ensure public safety and keep footpaths unobstructed. Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said DBKL officers and enforcement teams would conduct frequent ground inspections, including at night, to enforce safety clearances and check mandatory compliance stickers. Fadlun said enforcement of the updated guidelines would be stricter to ensure customer and pedestrian safety.

items.title: MetMalaysia, Nadma discuss cloud seeding amid haze, falling dam levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) is discussing another cloud-seeding operation with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) amid worsening haze and declining water levels at several dams. MetMalaysia deputy director-general (Operations) Ambun Dindang said the operation was being considered to increase water levels at dams, while rainfall generated could also help reduce the impact of the haze. "MetMalaysia is discussing with Nadma to carry out another cloud-seeding operation in the near future.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines -September 15, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: Trade talks begin Malaysia and Maldives agreed to begin negotiations on a preferential trade agreement, aiming to expand bilateral trade, investment and business opportunities. Muhyiddin vindicated Former PM Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said he felt vindicated after the High Court acquitted him of four Jana Wibawa charges, confident of innocence from the outset. RTS Link milestone The Johor Baru–Singapore RTS Link cleared a milestone with Woodlands North station completed, keeping the five‑minute cross‑border train on track for 2027 launch.

items.title: 11 Bangladeshis held over fake employment pass syndicate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has busted a syndicate providing electronic Temporary Employment Visit Passes (e-PLKS) and fake police reports at a commercial area in Jalan Chan Sow Lin. Its director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said 11 Bangladeshis believed to be the syndicate masterminds were arrested during the raids. "Also seized were 10 Bangladesh international passports, along with several printed e-PLKS documents and suspected fake police reports," he said.

items.title: Pahang Sultan decrees mosques hold special prayers for rain amid worsening haze
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang has decreed that the Pahang Mufti and all mosques perform Solat Hajat (special prayers) and Solat Sunat Istisqa' (prayers for rain) to seek divine relief from the haze. The Kesultanan Pahang Facebook page said the ruler hoped the people of Pahang, particularly Muslims, would join the prayers for rain to bring blessings, clear the air and end the haze affecting several areas. Kuantan experienced severe haze today, with API readings reaching their highest levels in recent weeks as conditions worsened across the country.

items.title: Selangor may postpone PSRA if haze worsens, says Amirudin
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor state government may postpone the Primary Religious School Assessment (PSRA) next week if the haze worsens in the state. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the government and Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) would monitor the situation. Amirudin, who is also the state education committee chairman, said the state government had parameters to determine follow-up action on the haze, including closing schools if API readings exceed 200.

items.title: Ringgit ends lower against US dollar as investors await FOMC decision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended lower against the US dollar on Tuesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the two-day US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which begins tonight, an analyst said. "Consequently, the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.25 per cent to 99.641 points while the 10-year US Treasury note yield surpassed the 5.00 per cent level. Other Asian currencies such as the Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht and Singapore dollar were also weaker against the US dollar," he told Bernama today.

items.title: 4 children drowned in Kulim laid to rest in single grave
items.summary: KULIM: The bodies of four children who drowned in a drain at Taman Desa Kayangan, Sungai Karangan, here, were laid to rest in a single grave. Earlier, the bodies of Muhammad Aeril Aziz Muhamad Zafis, 12; his half-brother, Muhammad Arif Naufan Abdullah, eight; and Muhammad Iman Nuruddin Khairol Anuar, 10, were brought to the Taman Desa Kayangan Surau at 3.26pm to allow family members and friends to pay their last respects. The body of another victim, Muhammad Zafril Arsyad Muhamad Azrin, 12, was taken to his family home in Kampung Baru Gajah Merangkak.

items.title: DAP: A-G must explain decision to discontinue case against Muhyiddin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General must provide a detailed explanation for his decision to discontinue part of the prosecution against former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, said DAP. DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo said transparency was essential as the case was of significant public interest. Gobind said public confidence in the A-G and the integrity of the criminal justice system as a whole would be severely eroded if active, high-profile prosecutions were discontinued midway without clear justification and a full explanation to the public.

items.title: Johari represents Malaysia at exchange of Islamic affairs, defence MoUs with Maldives
items.summary: The MoU on cooperation in Islamic affairs was exchanged with Maldivian Islamic Affairs Minister Dr Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed. A separate MoU on defence cooperation was exchanged with the Maldivian defence minister. Anwar said that as a maritime nation, Maldives places particular importance on maritime cooperation, including security and training.

items.title: Viral meal at Bukit Mertajam Hospital was afternoon tea, not main meal
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The viral meal photo involving medical officers on call at Bukit Mertajam Hospital (HBM) showed an afternoon tea serving, not a main meal, the Penang Health Department said. The department said the serving was one of four meals provided throughout the day — breakfast, lunch, afternoon tea and dinner. The meals were planned by HBM's Dietetics and Food Services Department, with menus prepared by dietitians and food preparation assistant officers based on the Health Ministry's Hospital Diet, Dietetics and Food Services Manual.

items.title: King, Queen urge Malaysians to wear masks amid haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's King and Queen, Their Majesties Sultan Ibrahim and Raja Zarith Sofiah, have advised the public to take precautions and wear face masks amid unhealthy air quality caused by the haze. In a statement shared on the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's official Facebook account, Their Majesties said unhealthy air quality could affect public health and cause various problems, particularly those involving the respiratory system. Their Majesties also advised Malaysians to reduce outdoor activities, particularly when Air Pollutant Index (API) readings reach unhealthy levels.

items.title: TNB – Automatic fuel adjustment does not cause sudden hike in electricity bills
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) has clarified that the automatic fuel adjustment (AFA) does not cause a sudden increase in electricity bills, following concerns raised by some consumers on the rising bills. "Since the implementation of the new electricity tariff, consumers have received AFA rebates for nine consecutive months, from August 2025 to April 2026," it said. TNB said that since the AFA was introduced, consumers have received greater benefits, with a total of RM3.1 billion in AFA rebates compared with RM0.8 billion in AFA surcharges.

items.title: China warns against space 'battlefield' after US says weapons deployed
items.summary: "The US has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action," a US Space Force spokesperson said in a statement that did not provide specifics on the weapons. Russia called Tuesday for space to be kept "free of any weapons." - WHY DOES THE US WANT WEAPONS IN SPACE?

items.title: Pestec disputes winding-up petition by SPECO over alleged corporate guarantee
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The board of directors of Pestec International Bhd has disputed a winding-up petition purportedly presented against the company by Shandong Power Equipment Company Limited (SPECO), maintaining that the company has not been validly served with the legal notice. The company was made aware of the petition after Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd emailed the company a copy of a notice of advertisement published by SPECO in two publications regarding the purported winding-up petition, on Sept 8. Based on the information available to Pestec, the petition stems from an alleged sum owed by the company under an undated corporate guarantee.

items.title: Capital A appoints PCCO managing partner as independent director
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Capital A Bhd has appointed Chuah Sue Yin as independent and non-executive director effective today. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Capital A said that Chuah holds a registered auditor license approved by the Finance Ministry. Besides Capital A, Chuah holds director positions at BP Plastics Holding Bhd and Tokio Marine Life Insurance Malaysia Bhd.

items.title: What is Jana Wibawa?
items.summary: It is a dedicated development programme for genuine Bumiputera contractors, whereby the members of the board of directors, shareholders and other relevant parties are 100 per cent Bumiputera. The programme aims to accelerate the implementation of government projects and enhance the capacity of Bumiputera contractors in the construction industry. First phase: The committee at the MOF level ensures that all criteria are met by prospective Bumiputera contractors.

items.title: Eco World's Singapore unit bidding for Urban Redevelopment Authority land for RM667.6mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Eco World Development Group Bhd announced that its unit Eco World Development (S) Pte Ltd had submitted a bid for a parcel of leasehold land at Lorong Punting / Sin Ming Avenue in Singapore. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Eco World said that Eco World Singapore has put in a bid of S$208.1 million (approximately RM667.62 million) for the 4,283 sq metres land to the Urban Redevelopment Authority on Sept 15. The decision on the award of the tender will be made after all bids have been evaluated, said Eco World.

items.title: PAC begins review on implementation of TH RCI recommendations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) today began proceedings on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to assess progress in implementing recommendations made in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution. Its chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the nearly four-hour session involved the senior deputy secretary-general of the Prime Minister's Department, which oversees TH, as well as the institution's chief executive officer and senior management. Mas Ermieyati said PAC would recall some of today's witnesses for further clarification and called in the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs), representatives from the finance ministry , agencies under the Prime Minister's Department and Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd.

items.title: MACC officer retracts police report against Muhyiddin’s lawyer; court decides not to cite for contempt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The High Court today decided not to begin contempt of court proceedings against Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation officer Mazery Mohd Zaini, as it accepted the officer’s explanations about his MACC colleague’s police report. Earlier today, former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s lawyers had accused Mazery of contempt of court, due to his actions that led to the police report. Muhyiddin’s lawyers had pointed out that Mazery was still testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s trial, and should not have communicated with anyone including the MACC colleague who lodged the police report.

items.title: Tour bus catches fire on North-South Expressway, 15 escape unhurt
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Fifteen people, including a tour bus driver, escaped unhurt after the vehicle carrying 14 passengers caught fire along the North-South Expressway near Yong Peng. The driver and tour leader managed to evacuate all passengers before firefighters arrived. Yong Peng Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Muhammad Amier Syah Hamzah said the department received a distress call at 1.37pm and dispatched nine firefighters to the scene.

items.title: Indonesian man first jailed for littering
items.summary: Johor Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said the 36‑year‑old general worker committed the offence in Stulang last February. "The man will undergo a six‑hour Community Service Order (CSO) upon completing his jail sentence," Zainal Fitri said at a press conference after inspecting the implementation of the 50th Series of CSO here today. Zainal Fitri said the cases resulted in total fines of RM71,550, with CSOs ranging from two to 10 hours.

items.title: NST columnist Datuk Rahim Mydin dies aged 75
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: New Straits Times columnist Datuk Abdul Rahim Mydin died today after a long battle with lung fibrosis. In 2024, Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah, conferred him the Darjah Dato' Paduka Mahkota Perak (DPMP), which carries the title Datuk. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Prosecution closes Muhyiddin's Jana Wibawa case after calling 29 witnesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The prosecution today closed its case against former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin after calling 29 witnesses to testify at the High Court here on charges of using his position to obtain bribes. Wan Shaharuddin also informed the court that six prosecution witnesses would be made available should the Bersatu president be called to enter his defence. "The six witnesses are Datuk Dr Marzuki Mohamad, Adam Radlan Muhammad Adam Muhammad, Asmar Asmadi Abdullah Sani, Datuk Seri Asri Hamidon, Datuk Mohd Ayob Mohd Ali and Mohd Shahmeizy Sulong," he said.

items.title: Johor SWCorp probes alleged Singapore waste dumping
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Johor SWCorp is preparing four investigation papers into the alleged dumping of construction waste from Singapore at several locations in Pontian last month. Its director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said no new dumping sites had been identified in Johor, while investigations involving four landowners were expected to take about three months before the papers were referred to the deputy public prosecutor for further action. Last month, construction debris believed to have originated from Singapore was found dumped at several locations in Pontian, including Kampung Sungai Karang.

items.title: Young Malaysians seek better jobs, affordable homes
items.summary: She said higher prices of goods, rent, transport and daily necessities were placing increasing pressure on young people, particularly those entering the workforce. Iman said she hoped the next five years would bring better employment opportunities and salaries that better matched the qualifications and skills of young Malaysians. Her biggest hope was for Malaysia to become a country that offers fairer opportunities to the younger generation.

items.title: PTT subsidiary bags RM83.26m earthworks contract from Sime Darby Property
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PTT's wholly-owned subsidiary, Pembinaan Tetap Teguh Sdn Bhd (PTTSB), has secured a letter of award (LOA) worth RM83.26 million from Sime Darby Property (BBR Business Park) Sdn Bhd. Specifically, the project covers Package 6 (i34), Package 7 (Main Linkage Road), and Package 8 (i26 and i28), PTT stated in an exchange filing. The overall project is slated for completion by March 28, 2028, with an earlier completion date of Sept 28, 2027, set for Package 6 (Advance Unit for i34).

items.title: [UPDATED] MB: I have no power to remove Negri ruler
items.summary: In a statement issued after today's state executive council meeting, Datuk Ismail Lasim said the matter must be determined based on the Negri Sembilan Constitution and the principles of constitutional monarchy, rather than political or personal considerations. Ismail said the position and processes concerning the Yang di-Pertuan Besar were specifically provided for under the state's Constitution. He said a proclamation did not, by itself, create constitutional authority.

items.title: Ringgit slides against euro, yen and pound as greenback gains momentum
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The ringgit ended lower against the US dollar on Tuesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the two-day US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which begins tonight, an analyst said. “Consequently, the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.25 per cent to 99.641 points while the 10-year US Treasury note yield surpassed the 5.00 per cent level. Other Asian currencies such as the Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht and Singapore dollar were also weaker against the US dollar,” he told Bernama today.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain warning issued for 10 states, KL until 9pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in 10 states and Kuala Lumpur until 9pm today. In Kedah, the affected areas are Sik, Kuala Muda, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap and Baling. In Selangor, the areas affected are Hulu Langat, Gombak, Hulu Selangor, Sabak Bernam and Kuala Selangor, as well as the entire Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: SWCorp: Investigation papers on construction waste dumping from Singapore to be ready in three months
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 15 – The Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) is currently finalising four investigation papers on the dumping of construction waste from Singapore in Pontian. Johor SWCorp director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said that the investigation papers are expected to be completed in three months time before being referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further action. Zainal Fitri was commenting on SWCorp’s investigation progress into the alleged dumping of construction waste from Singapore in Pontian.

items.title: Haze: 39 areas hit unhealthy API levels as of 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — A total of 39 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today. Two areas in Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings, namely Serian (171) and Samarahan (151). Meanwhile, 29 areas nationwide recorded moderate API levels.

items.title: Kelana Jaya line operations back on track after morning signal fault
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Rapid KL’s Kelana Jaya Line, which was disrupted by a signalling fault this morning, has returned to normal operations and is running according to schedule. Following the incident, its operations and technical teams took immediate action to restore the affected system and conducted continuous monitoring to ensure operations returned to normal as soon as possible. “Following the action taken, operations on the Kelana Jaya Line have returned to normal, and all trains are operating according to schedule,” it said.

items.title: Muhyiddin relieved after acquittal on four charges, hopes to be freed from three remaining charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin today expressed relief after the High Court decided to acquit him on four charges involving Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd. Muhyiddin expressed hope that he would also be freed of the remaining three charges that he is still facing in this trial. Muhyiddin’s lawyers had urged for Muhyiddin to be acquitted on those four charges instead.

items.title: Lawyer Haniff Khatri says decades of legal notes and 28 years of memories lost in Country Homes house fire
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Three decades of handwritten journals, irreplaceable legal notes, and 28 years of family memories were reduced to ash early today after a devastating fire gutted the home of prominent lawyer Mohamed Haniff Khatri Abdulla in Bandar Country Homes. The blaze, which broke out around 3am, completely consumed the upper floor of the residence, incinerating beds, clothing, home appliances, and personal archives that Haniff had accumulated over more than 30 years of legal practice, NST reported. His son, Mohamed Hamzah Khatri Mohamed Haniff, sifted through the wreckage to find a handheld gaming console on his bedroom floor, one of the few items to survive the flames.

items.title: Negeri MB insists has no unilateral power over Yang Di-Pertuan Besar, but stays silent on alleged proclamation signing
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 15 — Negeri Sembilan Mentri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim insisted today that he has no unilateral power over the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir, but stopped short of confirming or denying that he signed a disputed document at the centre of a growing constitutional row. The state executive council, which Ismail chairs, said in a statement that questions over the so-called Instrument of Proclamation must be resolved strictly under the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 (UUTKNS) and the principle of constitutional monarchy, "not as a political or personal matter." The statement comes after the Undang Yang Empat — the state's four ruling chiefs — and other traditional leaders publicly alleged that Ismail signed a proclamation on August 3effecting the dethronement of Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: Malaysia agrees in principle to support Maldives’ US$100m soft loan request, says Anwar
items.summary: MALE, Sept 15 — Malaysia has agreed in principle to support the Maldives’ application for a US$100 million (US$1=RM4.07) financing facility, which Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described as a form of soft loan to be implemented through both countries’ monetary authorities. Anwar said that the terms and mechanism for the facility are still being worked out by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA). “The President has written to me about the need to get our central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, to respond to the Maldivian request, precisely (from) the Maldives Monetary Authority, for this US$100 million facility.

items.title: Anwar says Malaysia, Maldives to expand cooperation in maritime security, halal and haj
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that as a maritime nation, the Maldives placed particular importance on maritime cooperation, including security and training. On Islamic affairs, Anwar said the Maldives’ status as an Islamic country provided opportunities to deepen cooperation in areas including halal, dakwah, Muslim affairs, waqf and haj. “Today we witnessed the exchange of new cooperation agreements in two important areas, which are defence cooperation and Islamic faith.

items.title: Muhyiddin trial: Prosecution completes case after 29 witnesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The prosecution today completed its case in former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's power abuse trial after calling in 29 prosecution witnesses, which means that the trial will now move on to the next stage. Lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin this afternoon told the High Court that the prosecution closes its case, and that the prosecution will offer six witnesses that Muhyiddin could call in as his witnesses if he is ordered to defend himself in this case. "With that, the prosecution closes this case.

items.title: Four of seven missing anglers found safe off Sekinchan, search continues for three
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 15 — Four of the seven anglers reported missing yesterday were found safe by a local fishing boat in the waters off Sekinchan, 25 nautical miles from the coast of Sungai Besar, at about 9.50 am today. Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director Abdul Muhaimin Muhammad Salleh said the four men were found floating close to one another and were in a weak condition. He said the search and rescue operation was ongoing to locate the remaining three victims, with the maritime search area expanded to 203.5 square nautical miles, while the aerial search covers 764 square nautical miles.

items.title: Babysitter pleads not guilty to exposing toddler to conditions that could have caused death
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 15 — A babysitter pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of exposing a 13-month-old boy under her care to conditions that could have caused his death last week. Noraidah Khairuddin, 44, entered the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Irwan Suainbon. According to the charge, Noraidah, as a person having custody of the toddler, was accused of exposing him in a manner that could have caused his death.

items.title: KL police propose KK Mart stores as safety points to boost crime prevention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The Kuala Lumpur Police propose making KK Mart convenience stores as Go-To-Safety-Point (GTSP) locations through a strategic collaboration with the company to strengthen crime monitoring and prevention efforts in the capital. “We see that KK Mart can be made a safety point for the surrounding community. Meanwhile, Fadil said that the KK Mart branch at the Kuala Lumpur IPK is the first convenience store branch in the PDRM building.

items.title: Anwar moots Malaysia-Maldives joint commission in KL this year
items.summary: MALÉ, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has proposed convening the Malaysia-Maldives Joint Commission in Kuala Lumpur before the end of this year to further advance bilateral relations between the two countries. Anwar said the Commission would be an important platform to address outstanding issues and translate the close relationship between Malaysia and the Maldives into concrete cooperation. Anwar said the Commission could also address issues affecting Maldivians in Malaysia, including students and those seeking healthcare.

items.title: Don’t rush: Home minister urges Malaysians to avoid MyKad replacement frenzy
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, Sept 15 — The people have been advised not to rush to replace their MyKad when applications for the new version open on Sept 17, to avoid congestion at National Registration Department (NRD) offices. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the replacement exercise for the new MyKad, which comes with about 50 additional security features, would be carried out in phases, while existing cards would remain valid for daily transactions. “I would like to advise people not to rush to replace their MyKad.

items.title: Prosecution drops four charges against Muhyiddin, presses on with three in corruption trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The High Court today acquitted former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin of four charges involving Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd's funds, as the prosecution today said it does not want to proceed with trial on those charges for now. High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin delivered her decision this afternoon on whether to only grant a DNAA or to acquit Muhyiddin on those four charges. “So with that, the court discharges and acquits the accused from those four charges only.

items.title: Ipsos poll: Malaysians prioritise jobs and homes over traditional milestones
items.summary: Specifically, 67 per cent of Malaysians identify a stable job as essential, compared to 65 per cent globally, while 60 per cent view home ownership as a key milestone, slightly above the global average of 58 per cent. Parenthood and marriage are viewed as markers of success by 47 per cent and 42 per cent of Malaysians, respectively, far outpacing global figures of 31 per cent and 25 per cent. Home ownership follows closely, cited by 64 per cent of Millennials and 55 per cent of Gen Z.

items.title: Muhyiddin trial: Lawyer accuses MACC officer of ‘intimidation’ over police report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad today told the High Court that a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer had allegedly attempted to intimidate and tarnish his reputation as a lawyer, based on the officer’s MACC colleague’s police report. Amer, who was cross-examining MACC officer Mazery Mohd Zaini as the 29th prosecution witness yesterday in Muhyiddin’s power abuse trial, said the police report had false information. Amer said the police report lodged yesterday had named him and referred to the ongoing trial, and referred to an alleged classified document that Muhyiddin’s lawyers had wanted to be included as evidence in the trial.

items.title: Police receive two reports over Negeri Sembilan MB’s alleged forced signing of royal document
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 15 — Police have received two reports concerning the Proclamation document allegedly signed under duress by Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, seeking to remove the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said following the reports lodged by the Menteri Besar, the police would classify the case to determine the appropriate direction and scope of the investigation. “I can confirm that two police reports were lodged by the Menteri Besar. It is our duty, upon receiving the reports, to classify them based on the nature and direction of the investigation.

items.title: Pesta Pulau Pinang returns, but moves to Tasek Gelugor after 50 Years at Sungai Nibong
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 15 — Pesta Pulau Pinang will return this year for a month-long celebration starting December 1, with the event relocating to Padang Menora in Tasek Gelugor. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow confirmed that while the annual event continues as scheduled, it will be held at a more compact venue compared to its traditional site in Sungai Nibong. The state government had explored several alternative locations before the Penang Regional Development Authority (Perda) offered the Tasek Gelugor site.

items.title: Fadhlina urges parents to screen children early for autism, ADHD and learning difficulties
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Sept 15 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) is encouraging parents to bring their children for screening programmes aimed at detecting learning difficulties, including autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), at an early stage. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the screening programmes are crucial to ensuring children with learning difficulties receive appropriate intervention and support. Fadhlina said the services include speech therapy and psychological assessments to evaluate children’s overall development.

items.title: Anwar receives 21-gun salute as Maldives rolls out red carpet for Malaysian PM
items.summary: MALE, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was accorded a full ceremonial welcome here today, marking the start of his official programme during his two-day visit to the Maldives. The Prime Minister, who is also Finance Minister, was accompanied by Maldives Minister of Islamic Affairs Dr Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed, who is the minister-in-attendance for the visit. Also present at the welcoming ceremony were Malaysian Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam.

items.title: Two detained after KPDN foils 2,400-litre diesel misappropriation attempt in Senai
items.summary: Johor KPDN director Lilis Saslinda Pornomo said the operation followed information and intelligence on diesel purchases suspected of violating the Control of Supplies Act 1961. Enforcement personnel found a suspicious lorry equipped with a storage tank and related equipment, filling diesel directly into the tank. KPDN also seized 15 fleet cards and five receipts or invoices related to the fuel purchases,” Lilis Saslinda said in a statement.

items.title: Police nab two ex-convicts in Johor over 11 cases involving housebreaking, robbery and theft
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 15 — Two ex-convicts who were released three years ago have been rearrested for their alleged involvement in 11 separate criminal cases, including housebreaking, robbery and theft, in the district recently. Iskandar Puteri acting police chief Superintendent Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said the two male suspects, aged 26 and 27, were arrested in the Tanjung Kupang and Kangkar Pulai areas on Sept 5. He said the arrests were made following a police report lodged on Sept 4 regarding a break-in at Forest City Starview in Gelang Patah.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng’s call to drop Umno from Penang govt not DAP stance, says Chow Kon Yeow
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Sept 15 — Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow stressed that DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng’s call for Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi to urge Penang PH to drop Umno from the state government does not represent the party’s official position. “It is not the party’s position (Lim Guan Eng’s challenge to Ahmad Zahid). Earlier, Guan Eng challenged Ahmad Zahid to urge Penang PH to drop Umno from the state government.

items.title: Former construction manager claims trial over RM14,000 CBT involving Tabung Haji project
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 15 — A former construction project manager pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving penalty collection totalling RM14,000 from a contractor for a commercial building project owned by Lembaga Tabung Haji. Mohamad Hashim Mukhatap, 53, then the Construction Manager for THP Timur Sdn Bhd, was charged with misappropriating the funds—collected as penalties from the contractor, Kelpile Sdn Bhd—by depositing them into his personal bank account. The case involves a proposed project to construct and complete a 22-storey commercial building comprising serviced apartments (244 units), penthouses (four units), public amenities, commercial space, parking facilities, a sub-basement (one level), and related facilities on Lot 273, Section 12, Kota Bharu.

items.title: Four Chinese nationals claim trial over alleged kidnapping of woman in Alor Setar
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Sept 15 — Three men and a woman, all of Chinese nationality, pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of kidnapping a fellow national last month. Huang Jian, 39; Wang Hao Yu, 33; Guan Siqi, 24; and Liu Tingjun, 46, entered their pleas after the charge was read out to them in Mandarin before Judge N. Priscilla Hemamalini. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nasruna Anhar Nordien appeared for the prosecution, while Guan Siqi was represented by lawyer S. Suresh, and the other three accused by lawyer Jodia Poh Yi Tying.

items.title: Queen Raja Zarith Sofiah orders postponement of Johor Family Day Carnival amid worsening haze
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 15 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, yesterday instructed that the Johor Family Day Carnival, scheduled for Sept 16, be postponed to a suitable date following the worsening haze situation in the state. According to a post uploaded on the Facebook page of Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar, Her Majesty instructed that the carnival be held when air quality improves. Insya-Allah, this carnival will be held when air quality returns to a good level,” Her Majesty said.

items.title: Dzulkefly: 902 health clinics nationwide to offer AI-assisted lung screening by year-end
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — A total of 902 health clinics nationwide will be empowered with Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted lung disease screening by the end of this year, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad. He said the step to strengthen lung health is crucial given that respiratory diseases currently account for one in five deaths globally. In this regard, Dr Dzulkefly praised the decade-long contributions of the NIHR Global Health Research Unit on Respiratory Health (RESPIRE) in driving public health research.
